summary: Pier light at the end of Sheboygan's north breakwater on Lake Michigan: lit 1900, moved from the old north pier in 1915, declared surplus by the Coast Guard in 2025.

structures.note: Steel tower raised on the north pier in 1904 per LighthouseFriends; the station record's 1905 comes from Wikidata and is not a source cited here. Moved without dismantling to the breakwater in 1915. Riveted steel plates; fourth-order helical-bar lantern in the 1917 description.
Timber crib built by the US Engineers, capped by a concrete block 25 by 30 ft, top 10 ft above lake level.

facts.agency: United States Coast Guard (owner at the 2025 excess notice)

access.note: Tower closed to visitors (LighthouseFriends). Coast Guard property, declared excess in 2025 and offered under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act. Any eligible owner needs a lease from the Army Corps of Engineers to use the pier.

events.note: Fixed red lens lantern on a wooden post at the south-east end of the breakwater, 24 October 1900
Enclosed tower, first shown 14 November 1902, per LighthouseFriends (the station record does not list it)
Steel tower raised at the outer end of the north pier, per LighthouseFriends; station record says 1905
Breakwater light listed among changes in the Bulletin's 1912 list (acetylene)
Steel tower moved without dismantling from the old north pier to the new breakwater; LighthouseFriends gives 19 August 1915
Harbour works complete; lights rearranged; system in commission 24 November 1916
First-class air siren established; 6-inch automatic siren, 3 s blast in 30 s
Illuminant changed from acetylene to electric incandescent
Lumber schooner Lottie Cooper wrecked near the Life-Saving Service station at Sheboygan; one crew member drowned
Keeper G. M. S. Hansen rescued two men from a capsized boat (Bulletin notes; scrambled scan, check page image)
Keeper Ingvald Olsen and helper pulled a boy from thin ice (LighthouseFriends)
Declared excess by the Coast Guard; offered at no cost under the NHLPA; letters of interest due 1 September 2025
City of Sheboygan resolution (dated 23 February 2026) authorising an application to purchase; GSA control 1-U-WI-630

wrecks.outcome: Lumber schooner (252 tons, from Advance, Michigan, for Sheboygan) capsized near the Life-Saving Service station. The Service's report gives a crew of five; the crew got onto the deckload of lumber, and Edward Olsen drowned trying to reach the shore on a raft of lumber. LighthouseFriends gives seven crew, six clinging to the rigging and rescued, and spells the drowned man's name Olson.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends dates the steel tower that stands on the breakwater to 1904, when it was raised on the north pier. The station record's 1905 is from Wikidata, not a source cited here. No primary source read settles the year, so the story gives 1904 as LighthouseFriends' date only.

The 1917 Commissioner's description gives a flashing red light every four seconds (fifth-order lens). LighthouseFriends says the light now flashes white every four seconds. The station record's Fl R 4s is not confirmed by a Light List read here.

notes_for_editor: 1) No keepers are sourced to the tower's early years beyond the LighthouseFriends lists; the roster is as printed by LighthouseFriends, with the Carpenter note. 2) LighthouseFriends' breakwater list starts in 1873 with John H. Roberts and Peter Danielsen, before the breakwater light existed (first shown 1900). That list may be the pierhead's; the story says only that it starts before the light. 3) The Carpenter disagreement (pierhead 1866-1903 in the text; breakwater 1886-1903 in the list) is stated in the story. 4) The 1914 Bulletin (PDF p. 36, printed p. 132, 'Saving of life and property') was checked on the page image: 'On August 17 G. M. S. Hansen, keeper of the Sheboygan Breakwater Light and Sheboygan Pierhead Light Station, Wis., rescued two men from a capsized boat.' The index (1912-1917, PDF p. 19) gives 'Hansen, G.M. S., keeper Sheboygan Breakwater, rescue 132', matching the printed page. 5) The 1912-1917 index names Robert H. Paul (keeper, Sheboygan Pierhead) and Paul G. Pitscher (assistant); LighthouseFriends names Robert E. Paul and Paul G. Pitschler. Not linked: initials and spellings differ. 6) The steel tower date: LighthouseFriends 1904; the station record's 1905 comes from Wikidata (not a source cited here). The story gives 1904 as LighthouseFriends' date only. Lighthouse Board reports for 1904-1905 are not in the local corpus. 7) Light character: the 1917 Commissioner description gives a red fifth-order light (flashing every 4 s); LighthouseFriends says white now; the station record says Fl R 4s. No Light List entry for this light was read (Lake Michigan volume not checked). 8) The 1917 Commissioner description is on printed p. 86 (scan p. 297), in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1917 ('in commission November 24, 1916' falls in that fiscal year). 9) Crew of the Lottie Cooper: the Life-Saving Service report gives 'a crew of five men'; LighthouseFriends gives seven crew (six rescued from the rigging, one drowned). Both are stated in the story. The spelling Olsen (Service) and Olson (LighthouseFriends) is noted. 10) The 1894 wreck is dated 9 April 1894 by both sources. The breakwater light did not exist then (first shown 24 October 1900); the story says so. 11) Chronicling America searches (Sheboygan with lighthouse and keeper, Wisconsin papers 1900-1925) returned 126 hits, none read as relevant; a phrase search for the breakwater light returned none. 12) USLHS lists this place as a minor aid with no roster. 13) Sheboygan Press articles (January 2026, July 2025) returned HTTP 403 and were not read; the city application is taken from the resolution itself (checked: resolution 170-25-26, dated February 23, 2026). 14) Verification 2026-10-28: removed the 'station record gives 1905' disagreement (a Wikidata figure, not a source); removed the unsourced 'same keepers seem to have tended' inference, 'fog signal came last', 'may be a list of the pierhead's keepers' guess; removed 'best-known' and 'fullest contemporary account' superlatives; 'boys' changed to 'local miscreants' (LF); 'cutting' to 'inscribing'; 'a sea froze the door shut' changed to driven snow and sleet; NOAA quote cited to LighthouseFriends only (not the 1917 report); the 1914 footnote labelled as 'Saving of life and property'; added footnote to the opening sentence; metres added; 'surplus' changed to 'excess' (the notice's word); the 1916 Bulletin's planned fog signal described as planned; the 1894 wreck is no longer placed at the 'harbour mouth the breakwater light marks' (the light was not yet lit).
